unit.title: Models with numbers: variables, constraints, objective

lesson.title: The best plan is at a corner
lesson.subtitle: Linear programming in two dimensions, on graph paper

video.title: The best plan is at a corner
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Salma Haddad — secondary maths teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor Eze — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor in the school garden with a watering can; empty beds marked out with string.
scenes.animation: Tomato and bean signs pop up on the beds; a question mark appears.
scenes.narration: Our school garden: tomato beds sell for thirty coins, bean beds for forty. But land, water and the pupils’ hours are all limited. How many of each should we plant?

scenes.visual: Title card with the Darsi mark and the Optimization track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; title slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: The best plan is at a corner
scenes.narration: Today: linear programming in two dimensions. Draw the plans, and find the best one at a corner.

scenes.visual: Four lines of the model type out on a card, each beside a small icon: land, water, hours, coins.
scenes.animation: Each line types in as it is said.
scenes.narration: Call the tomato beds x and the bean beds y. Land: x plus y, at most eight. Water: two x plus y, at most fourteen cans a day. Hours: x plus three y, at most eighteen a week. Profit: thirty x plus forty y.

scenes.visual: Axes: tomato beds across, bean beds up. The land line is drawn from (8, 0) to (0, 8); the area below it shades lightly.
scenes.animation: The line draws itself; the shade spreads down towards the origin.
scenes.narration: On graph paper, each limit is a straight line. For land, the line joins eight beds of tomatoes to eight beds of beans. Plans on the line use all the land. Plans below it, towards zero, fit.

scenes.visual: The water and hours lines join the land line; the five-sided feasible region shades; its five corners ring.
scenes.animation: Lines draw in turn; the region fills; corner rings pop one by one.
scenes.narration: Draw all three lines, and shade where every limit holds. That shape holds every feasible plan. Its corners are where lines meet, such as six and two, or three and five.

scenes.visual: A dashed profit line crosses the shaded shape low down, then slides up, parallel, until it touches only one corner.
scenes.animation: The dashed line glides up in steps; the profit counter rises.
scenes.narration: Now the goal. Every plan earning, say, one hundred and twenty coins lies on one straight line. Slide that line up, and the profit grows. The last point of the shape it touches is the best plan.

scenes.visual: The dashed line rests on the corner (3, 5); a star lands there with 290.
scenes.animation: The corner pulses; the star pops; 290 counts up.
scenes.narration: Here it touches the corner three tomato beds and five bean beds: two hundred and ninety coins. Straight-line limits and a straight-line goal make a linear program. And its best plan is always at a corner.

scenes.visual: Ms Salma points at the middle of the shaded shape. Three answer cards drop in.
scenes.animation: Cards bounce in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! Why is the best plan at a corner, and not somewhere in the middle of the shape?

scenes.visual: The check lands on ‘You can still slide further’. A dot walks from corner to corner along the edges to (3, 5); the land and hours lines glow.
scenes.animation: The dot hops corner to corner; two lines glow; a small water can shows 3.
scenes.on_screen_text: From inside, you can still climb
scenes.narration: From any point inside, the profit line can still slide further. Push it to an edge, then along the edge to a corner. That’s why the simplex method walks only from corner to corner. At the best corner, land and hours are used up; water has three cans to spare.

scenes.visual: The tomato price tag changes from 30 to 50; the dashed line tilts; the star jumps from (3, 5) to (6, 2).
scenes.animation: The tag flips; the line rotates; the star hops.
scenes.on_screen_text: Change the price, change the corner
scenes.narration: Change what you value, and the best corner can change. With tomatoes at fifty coins, the best plan jumps to six and two: three hundred and eighty. The shape didn’t move; only the profit line tilted.

scenes.visual: Class signs on the beds; a new line ‘every class gets a bed’ is drawn, trimming the shape.
scenes.animation: Signs pop up; the new line draws; the shape shrinks a little.
scenes.narration: And profit isn’t the garden’s only goal. It’s also for learning: maybe every class should get a bed of each. Say so, and it becomes one more limit. Agree the goal before you trust the corner.

scenes.visual: A phone with the lab: the shaded garden plans, a dashed line and three sliders.
scenes.animation: A finger drags a slider; the dashed line slides up; the star moves.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: The best plan is at a corner
scenes.narration: In the app, drag the profit to aim for up, slowly, and watch where the dashed line leaves the shape. Then change a price or the hours, and see the best corner move.

scenes.visual: Mr Okafor holds up a pupils’ rota with more hours. Three answer cards appear.
scenes.narration: Your turn. If pupils could give twenty-four hours a week instead of eighteen, would the best plan stay at three and five?

scenes.visual: The answer card gets the check; four summary lines and a takeaway bar.
scenes.animation: Lines tick in; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: No: the hours line moves out, and the best plan becomes eight bean beds, three hundred and twenty coins. Remember: each limit is a line, the feasible plans are the shaded shape, and the best plan is at a corner. Move a limit or a price, and check again.

scenes.visual: Salma’s class with graph paper: lines drawn, corners circled, profits written beside them.
scenes.animation: Corners get circled one by one; one group stars the winner.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: give each group graph paper and the garden’s three limits. Pupils draw the lines, shade the plans that fit, and work out the profit at each corner. Which corner wins, and would they plant it?

checkpoints.prompt: Why is the best plan of a linear program at a corner?

options.text: Plans in the middle break a limit
From any inside point the profit line can still slide further

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — from inside you can always earn more, until you reach an edge, then a corner.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — plans inside the shape keep every limit, but the profit line can still slide past them. It stops only at a corner.

checkpoints.prompt: Pupils can give 24 hours a week instead of 18. Does the best plan stay at (3, 5)?

options.text: Yes: the best corner never moves
No: the hours line moves out, so the corners change
No: the profit per bed changes

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the hours line moves out, the shape changes, and the best plan becomes (0, 8): 320 coins.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — prices haven’t changed, but the hours line has moved, so the shape and its corners change. The best is now (0, 8), 320.
